# Data Codebook

832 simulated districts representing Texas, observed over seven years

The codebook is also on the [Data page](data.html#codebook)

## Codebook

**Each row represents one district in one year**

<table>
<thead><tr><th>Variable</th><th>Definition</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><code>state</code></td><td><ul><li>TX identifies the state represented by the simulation</li></ul></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>district_id</code></td><td><ul><li>Synthetic district identifier from 1 to 832</li><li>The same identifier follows a district across all seven years</li></ul></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>year</code></td><td><ul><li>Study year from 1 to 7</li><li>Not a calendar year</li></ul></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>cohort</code></td><td><ul><li>treated_year5, treated_year6, or never</li><li>The traditional DID dataset has no Year 6 cohort</li></ul></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>treatment_start_year</code></td><td><ul><li>First treated year is 5 or 6</li><li>0 means never treated</li></ul></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>treated_ever</code></td><td><ul><li>1 for a district that receives treatment during the study</li><li>0 for a never-treated district</li></ul></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>treated</code></td><td><ul><li>1 from the adoption year onward</li><li>0 before adoption and for never-treated districts</li></ul></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>event_time</code></td><td><ul><li>Study year minus adoption year</li><li>-1 is the year before adoption and 0 is the first treated year</li><li>Missing for never-treated districts</li></ul></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>outcome_std</code></td><td><ul><li>Simulated achievement measured in SD units</li><li>The full untreated Texas panel defines the reference mean and SD</li><li>Treatment effects are added after standardization</li><li>The observed outcome is not standardized again after treatment</li></ul></td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>

An effect of **0.20 SD** means an increase equal to one fifth of the reference standard deviation

## Generation

The generator follows the pure-data mechanism from our simulation paper using Texas's
SEDA-derived variance components and serial correlation. It adds a district baseline,
a shared year shock, and correlated district-year errors, standardizes the full untreated
panel, then assigns cohorts and adds effects. The seed is 20261014.

The traditional effect is 0.20 SD in every treated period. Early staggered adopters receive
0.10, 0.20, and 0.30 SD in Years 5-7. Late adopters receive 0.15 and 0.25 SD in Years 6-7.
The true Simple ATT is 0.20 SD in both datasets. Observed estimates will differ.
